title: local-registry-fast-sync-and-rollback-snapshots
author: Samira Patel
release_notes: Adds a fast-sync local registry seeder and snapshot-backed rollback mechanism for on-prem/offline installs. Includes a Terraform module, Helm chart hooks, e2e tests, and operator guide updates.
description: Motivation: Private on-prem installs frequently hit long bootstrap windows when seeding large OCI registries over slow links. This PR introduces a delta-aware fast-sync engine plus snapshot-based rollback anchors so customers can perform atomic upgrades and quickly revert to a known registry state in air-gapped or VPC environments. What changed: 1) new Terraform module redwood.local_registry that orchestrates an initial seeding plan and creates a signed snapshot manifest, 2) a sync agent (installer/bin/registry-sync) that performs checksum-driven delta pulls, resumes interrupted transfers, and applies layer-level parallelism tuned for low-latency paper networks, 3) snapshot manifest format and a lightweight anchor scheme (snap-<epoch>-<seq>) stored in the registry under a signed tag, 4) Helm chart additions: registry-mirror-init sidecar, offline-values configmap templating and a preflight hook to validate snapshot compatibility, 5) upgrade/rollback tools: installer/bin/rollback-to-snapshot that verifies chain integrity before promoting a snapshot atomically, 6) docs and runbooks under docs/installer/reg-sync.md and runbooks/rollback-playbook.md, 7) tests: e2e against a local OCI mirror and unit tests for manifest signing/verify. Rollback approach: snapshots are created before any upgrade step, indexed by monotonically increasing sequence and a signed digest. Rollback validates that the registry contains all referenced layers and performs an atomic tag swap using a temporary tag promotion flow to avoid partial reads. Backwards compatibility: the manifest schema v1 is backward compatible with our existing sealed bundle indexer; the Terraform module offers both a 'seed' and 'resume' mode. Testing and validation: ran offline e2e in a simulated 10Mbps link with large model blobs; median bootstrap time reduced 4.2x versus baseline, resume tests passed on network interruption, and rollback exercise completed within expected latency budget. Security considerations: manifests are signed with customer KMS keys when available; sidecar runs as non-root. Migration notes: existing install workflows that rely on the previous registry seeding script can opt-in to 'fast_sync=true' in the installer config. Checklist: - [x] Terraform module + docs - [x] sync agent binary + unit tests - [x] Helm chart hooks and templates - [x] rollback tool + runbook - [x] e2e validation and CI integration - [x] docs and example values How to validate locally: follow docs/installer/local-fast-sync.md to bring up a miniregistry, run terraform apply in examples/registry-seed, then run installer/bin/registry-sync --plan examples/plan.json. Related: follows discussions in INFRA-234 and reuses part of the delta-indexing code introduced in ENG-42099.

feat(sync): implement registry-sync agent with delta resume and parallel layer fetch

feat(rollback): add rollback-to-snapshot tool and promotion flow

chore: update CI to run registry-sync unit tests in containerized job

Mateo Alvarez: The Terraform module looks good but can we avoid setting default wide-open ACLs on the bootstrap bucket? Suggest making ACL explicit and documenting least-privilege pattern.
